human_visual_assessment: HINT removed thin scratches more cleanly and retained stronger local continuity.
MAT frequently retained thin lines or introduced pale fragmented structures.
HINT remained imperfect on some large and mixed losses.
selection_rationale: HINT won all twelve paired cases on eight of the nine selected anchors.
Its advantage covered reference, perceptual, feature, colour, texture and boundary evidence.
HINT completed all cases at native 768 by 768 resolution.
HINT's MIT software license is simpler for continued research reuse.
limitations: The purposive twelve-case pilot supports method selection, not a fourth full-benchmark claim.
Cases are nested within five paintings; painting is the independent unit.
Both released checkpoints are trained on photographic scene data rather than paintings.
The HINT 512 fallback and MAT 512 adapter introduce resampling into a 768-pixel benchmark.
Exact-mask compositing preserves observed pixels but can expose boundary mismatch.
Metrics are complementary diagnostic evidence; no universal quality or trustworthiness score is constructed.
Human visual review is required and may select neither method.
MAT carries a noncommercial research license; deployment or broader reuse requires license review.
Selection for expansion does not make HINT a conservation-approved method.
future_benchmark_role: Selected additional learned inpainting method for the planned 300-painting expansion.
